html:
Funan was a trading kingdom, or network of Indianised states, in the Mekong Delta of what is now southern Vietnam and Cambodia, from about the 1st to the 6th or 7th century CE. It is often called the first known kingdom of Southeast Asia.

Funan is a Chinese name. No local text from the period names the state, and most of what we know comes from Chinese reports, chief among them the account of Kang Tai and Zhu Ying, envoys of the Chinese kingdom of Eastern Wu who stayed there in the mid-3rd century. Later legend says it was founded when an Indian Brahmin, Kaundinya, married a local queen, Soma.

Its wealth came from its place on the sea route between India and China. Ships stopped on the coast to wait for the monsoon winds or to move goods across the Malay peninsula. The port of Óc Eo, dug up in the 1940s, has yielded Indian jewellery, Chinese bronze mirrors and even Roman coins of the Roman Empire. Canals linked the port to inland towns.

Hindu and Buddhist ideas, Sanskrit and Indian royal titles spread through Funan, a pattern later followed across the region. In the 6th century Funan was eclipsed by Chenla, a Khmer state further inland, and the sea routes moved south toward the Strait of Malacca, where Srivijaya later rose. Funan's lands later became part of the Khmer Empire, and its neighbour on the coast was Champa.
sum: Funan was a trading kingdom, or network of Indianised states, in the Mekong Delta of what is now southern Vietnam and Cambodia, from about the 1st to the 6th or 7th century CE. It is often called the first known kingdom of Southeast Asia.
